This notebook measures the incremental delivery overpayment when a BGE
customer moves from Schedule R before a heat-pump retrofit to Schedule RD
after the retrofit. It compares the same modeled building in two segments:

- **Before:** upgrade 00 on posted, uncalibrated Schedule R.
- **After:** upgrade 01 on posted, uncalibrated Schedule RD.

For each building, over/underpayment is the change in its delivery bill minus
the change in its allocated delivery marginal cost:

$$
\text{over/underpayment}
=
(B_{\mathrm{HP}} - B_{\mathrm{baseline}})
-
(MC_{\mathrm{HP}} - MC_{\mathrm{baseline}}).
$$

Positive values are overpayment; negative values are underpayment. Residual
cost is not part of this incremental metric.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import yaml
from great_tables import GT

from lib.great_tables import get_switchbox_gt_tab_options
from lib.quarto import display_gt
from lib.rates_analysis.rate_case_funcs import (
    HEATING_ORDER,
    add_heating_label,
    bat_component_delta,
    segment_upgrade,
    weighted_mean,
)
```

## Parameters

Batch identity lives in `batch_config.yaml`, keeping this notebook aligned
with the other Maryland rate-analysis notebooks.

```{python}
#| label: parameters

_batch_config = yaml.safe_load(Path("../batch_config.yaml").read_text())

STATE = _batch_config["STATE"]
BATCH = _batch_config["BATCH"]
UTILITY = "bge"
BILL_COL = "annual_bill_delivery"
MC_COL = "economic_burden_delivery"

SEGMENT_BEFORE = f"{_batch_config['BASELINE_BILL_SCENARIO']}_precalc"
SEGMENT_AFTER = "default_rd_uncalibrated_calibrated"
UPGRADE_BEFORE = segment_upgrade(STATE, BATCH, SEGMENT_BEFORE)
UPGRADE_AFTER = segment_upgrade(STATE, BATCH, SEGMENT_AFTER)

print(
    f"state={STATE}  utility={UTILITY}  batch={BATCH}\n"
    f"before={SEGMENT_BEFORE} (upgrade {UPGRADE_BEFORE:02d})\n"
    f"after={SEGMENT_AFTER} (upgrade {UPGRADE_AFTER:02d})"
)
```

## Compare delivery bills and marginal costs

We join the two master BAT segments by building ID. The underlying
`annual_bill_delivery` and `economic_burden_delivery` columns remain valid in
both stages even though calibrated-stage BAT and residual-allocation columns
do not. Homes that already had heat pumps in upgrade 00 are excluded because
they are not undergoing the modeled retrofit.

```{python}
#| label: compare-segments

payment = add_heating_label(
    bat_component_delta(
        STATE,
        BATCH,
        SEGMENT_BEFORE,
        SEGMENT_AFTER,
        components=[BILL_COL, MC_COL],
        utility=UTILITY,
    )
).with_columns(
    (
        pl.col(f"delta_{BILL_COL}") - pl.col(f"delta_{MC_COL}")
    ).alias("over_underpayment")
)

print(
    f"{payment.height:,} modeled buildings representing "
    f"{payment['weight'].sum():,.0f} BGE customers"
)
```

Let's inspect the columns used in the calculation:

```{python}
#| label: payment-sample

payment.select(
    "bldg_id",
    "heating_label",
    "weight",
    f"{BILL_COL}_before",
    f"{BILL_COL}_after",
    f"delta_{BILL_COL}",
    f"{MC_COL}_before",
    f"{MC_COL}_after",
    f"delta_{MC_COL}",
    "over_underpayment",
).head(8)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scenario-inventory
#| tbl-cap: "Master BAT segments used in the Schedule R-to-RD incremental overpayment analysis."

_inventory = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "period": ["Before retrofit", "After retrofit"],
        "segment": [SEGMENT_BEFORE, SEGMENT_AFTER],
        "upgrade": [UPGRADE_BEFORE, UPGRADE_AFTER],
        "tariff": ["Schedule R", "Schedule RD"],
    }
)

display_gt(
    GT(_inventory)
    .cols_label(
        period="Comparison",
        segment="Master BAT segment",
        upgrade="Upgrade",
        tariff="Tariff",
    )
    .fmt_number(columns="upgrade", decimals=0)
    .tab_source_note(
        f"Source: s3://data.sb/switchbox/cairo/outputs/hp_rates/"
        f"{STATE.lower()}/all_utilities/{BATCH}/."
    )
    .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
)
```

## Incremental overpayment by baseline heating type

We report weighted averages for each baseline heating type. The “All
fossil-fuel homes” row combines homes originally heated with natural gas, oil,
or propane—the population addressed by the expert-testimony overpayment
calculation.

```{python}
#| label: payment-summary

def summarize_payment(df: pl.DataFrame, label: str) -> dict[str, str | float]:
    return {
        "heating_type": label,
        "weighted_customers": float(df["weight"].sum()),
        "avg_bill_before": weighted_mean(df, f"{BILL_COL}_before"),
        "avg_bill_after": weighted_mean(df, f"{BILL_COL}_after"),
        "avg_bill_change": weighted_mean(df, f"delta_{BILL_COL}"),
        "avg_mc_before": weighted_mean(df, f"{MC_COL}_before"),
        "avg_mc_after": weighted_mean(df, f"{MC_COL}_after"),
        "avg_mc_change": weighted_mean(df, f"delta_{MC_COL}"),
        "avg_over_underpayment": weighted_mean(df, "over_underpayment"),
        "aggregate_over_underpayment_m": float(
            (df["over_underpayment"] * df["weight"]).sum()
        )
        / 1e6,
    }


available_heating = [
    label
    for label in HEATING_ORDER
    if label in payment["heating_label"].unique().to_list()
]
summary_rows = [
    summarize_payment(
        payment.filter(pl.col("heating_label") == label),
        label,
    )
    for label in available_heating
]

FOSSIL_HEATING = ["Natural gas", "Oil/propane"]
fossil_payment = payment.filter(pl.col("heating_label").is_in(FOSSIL_HEATING))
summary_rows.append(
    summarize_payment(fossil_payment, "All fossil-fuel homes")
)

payment_summary = pl.DataFrame(summary_rows)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-payment-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Incremental BGE delivery overpayment after moving from Schedule R before a heat-pump retrofit to Schedule RD afterward, by baseline heating type."

display_gt(
    GT(payment_summary)
    .cols_label(
        heating_type="Baseline heating type",
        weighted_customers="Customers",
        avg_bill_before="Bill before",
        avg_bill_after="Bill after",
        avg_bill_change="Bill change",
        avg_mc_before="MC before",
        avg_mc_after="MC after",
        avg_mc_change="MC change",
        avg_over_underpayment="Over/underpayment",
        aggregate_over_underpayment_m="Aggregate ($M)",
    )
    .fmt_number(columns="weighted_customers", decimals=0, use_seps=True)
    .fmt_currency(
        columns=[
            "avg_bill_before",
            "avg_bill_after",
            "avg_bill_change",
            "avg_mc_before",
            "avg_mc_after",
            "avg_mc_change",
            "avg_over_underpayment",
        ],
        decimals=0,
    )
    .fmt_number(columns="aggregate_over_underpayment_m", decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note(
        "Over/underpayment = change in delivery bill − change in delivery "
        "marginal cost. Positive values are overpayment."
    )
    .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
)
```

## Result for fossil-heated homes

```{python}
#| label: fossil-result

_fossil_result = payment_summary.filter(
    pl.col("heating_type") == "All fossil-fuel homes"
)
FOSSIL_BILL_CHANGE = float(_fossil_result["avg_bill_change"][0])
FOSSIL_MC_CHANGE = float(_fossil_result["avg_mc_change"][0])
FOSSIL_OVERPAYMENT = float(_fossil_result["avg_over_underpayment"][0])
FOSSIL_AGGREGATE_OVERPAYMENT_M = float(
    _fossil_result["aggregate_over_underpayment_m"][0]
)
```

When the average BGE fossil-heated home moves from Schedule R before the
heat-pump retrofit to Schedule RD afterward, its annual delivery bill increases
by **`{python} f"${FOSSIL_BILL_CHANGE:,.0f}"`** while its allocated annual
delivery marginal cost increases by **`{python} f"${FOSSIL_MC_CHANGE:,.0f}"`**.
The difference is an incremental delivery overpayment of
**`{python} f"${FOSSIL_OVERPAYMENT:,.0f}"` per year**, or
**`{python} f"${FOSSIL_AGGREGATE_OVERPAYMENT_M:,.1f} million"`** across the
modeled BGE fossil-heated population.

## Interpretation limits

- This comparison intentionally changes both the building upgrade and tariff:
  Schedule R on upgrade 00 to Schedule RD on upgrade 01. It therefore answers
  the customer transition specified above; it does not isolate the retrofit
  effect while holding the tariff fixed.
- Existing heat-pump homes are excluded because they do not undergo the
  modeled fossil-to-heat-pump conversion.
- Over/underpayment uses delivery bills and marginal-cost allocations only.
  Residual costs and Maryland OHEP discounts are outside this metric.
